reason: The hypothesis combines the established effect of Y/Hf doping on hot corrosion spallation in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA (P3, P5) with the concept of a diffusion-formed gradient interlayer for adhesion (P4, P14) and the high-entropy approach to CMAS resistance (P31), but substitutes Ce for Y/Hf and proposes a specific Ce-enriched gradient interlayer mechanism at the bond coat/TGO interface. This substitution is not directly studied or proposed in any passage; the passages only show Y/Hf co-doping effects and Zr/Hf gradient layers in different alloy systems. The hypothesis thus transfers the reactive element doping idea to a new element (Ce) and links it to a gradient interlayer mechanism for CMAS resistance, which is a synthesis of multiple sources into a new proposal.
